title: Selective Randomization Inference for Interference
abstract: arXiv:2611.02443v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Empirical researchers often use tests for interference as pretests or robustness checks. However, when the results guide the choice of models, parameters, or hypotheses, the resulting data-dependent selection can compromise the validity of subsequent inference. This paper develops a two-stage selective randomization inference framework for interference that explicitly conditions on the selection event to account for data-dependent selection. We first test the null hypothesis of no treatment spillover using a conditional randomization method. If this null is rejected, we test the null hypothesis of zero exposure contrast under a pre-specified exposure mapping that allows for spillover effects; otherwise, we test the null hypothesis of no direct effects under the assumption of no spillover. We prove that each second-stage test controls the selective Type I error rate in finite samples and evaluate the size and power of the proposed tests t

translated_title: 干扰效应的选择性随机化推断
translated_abstract: 实证研究者经常将干扰效应检验用作预检验或稳健性检查。然而，当检验结果用于指导模型、参数或假设的选择时，由此产生的依赖数据的选择可能会损害后续推断的有效性。本文针对干扰效应提出了一个两阶段选择性随机化推断框架，该框架显式地以选择事件为条件，以考虑这种数据依赖的选择。我们首先使用条件随机化方法检验“无处理溢出效应”的原假设。如果该原假设被拒绝，则在允许溢出效应的预设暴露映射下检验“暴露对比为零”的原假设；否则，在无溢出的假设下检验“无直接效应”的原假设。我们证明了每个第二阶段检验在有限样本中都能控制选择性第一类错误率，并评估了所提出检验的尺寸与功效。
tldr: 本文提出了一种针对干扰效应的两阶段选择性随机化推断框架，通过以数据驱动的选择事件为条件，在有限样本中控制选择性第一类错误率，从而保证经过模型或假设选择后后续推断仍然有效。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a two-stage selective randomization inference framework for interference that explicitly conditions on the selection event, thereby controlling the selective Type I error rate in finite samples when data-dependent choices of models, parameters, or hypotheses follow interference tests.
